item.title: Charlie Puth and Ellie Goulding Will Make Their India Debut in February 2027
item.dc:creator: Rolling Stone India
item.content:encoded:
American pop hitmaker Charlie Puth and British singer-songwriter Ellie Goulding will make their India debut at the inaugural edition of Johnnie & Co. Festival, performing on Feb. 13, 2027 at Mahalaxmi Racecourse in Mumbai.

The lineup for the festival also includes Indian pop artists such as Kayan, Gini, Mali, Taba Chake, with more to be announced. The performances mark a long-anticipated India debut for Puth, best known for songs like “See You Again” and “We Don’t Talk Anymore,” who released his latest album Whatever’s Clever! earlier this year. Goulding, who also released her latest album I Know Too Much in September this year, brings hits such as “Love Me Like You Do” and “Lights” to India as part of the festival.

Charlie Puth says in a statement, “I’ve heard so much about the energy of Indian fans, and I’m really excited to finally be performing in India for the first time. Music has always been about bringing people together, and I can’t wait to experience that with everyone in Mumbai. I’m looking forward to being there on 13 February, playing some of my favourite songs and being part of a night that celebrates the energy and connection that live music creates.”

The event details note that an age limit will be applied “as per Maharashtra excise rules,” while ticketing partner BookMyShow mentions that the event is open to all age groups. Tickets for the Johnnie & Co. Festival, produced and promoted by Team Innovation, will go live with an HSBC presale on Nov. 23, 2026 to Nov. 24, followed by general sales starting on Nov. 25, 2026 via BookMyShow.

item.title: Starting From Zero: xikers on Breaking Out of Their Own Universe With New Album
item.dc:creator: Debashree Dutta
item.content:encoded:
For most of their career so far, xikers have existed inside the HOUSE OF TRICKY.

Since debuting in 2023 with HOUSE OF TRICKY: Doorbell Ringing, the 10-member boy group comprising MINJAE, JUNMIN, SUMIN, JINSIK, HYUNWOO, JUNGHOON, SEEUN, YUJUN, HUNTER, and YECHAN has built one of the more distinctive narratives in contemporary K-pop. Rooted in science fiction and fantasy, it follows 10 young men navigating a labyrinth of illusions created by a trickster, which ultimately leads them to break free and choose their own path. Across the HOUSE OF TRICKY series, from Doorbell Ringing and HOW TO PLAY to later entries like WATCH OUT, SPUR, and WRECKING THE HOUSE, the band took listeners on a journey of adventure, chaos, and rebellion. The music shifted from release to release, drawing on hip-hop, EDM, rock, and pop influences, but the underlying spirit stayed the same as xikers kept evolving and pushing forward.

That consistency matters in an increasingly crowded generation. Every new group is trying to establish what makes them different. Some do it through intricate lore, others through a signature sound or performance style. But xikers have never fit quite neatly into a single box. On ROUTE ZERO: The CALLING, they channel that versatility into something more personal.

Across six tracks, the album is packed with plenty of range, from the explosive lead single “DIENAMITE” and the laid-back groove of “Go” to the frenetic “One” and the slower, reflective closer “Sanctuary,” the album steps away from fantasy world-building and leans into themes of self-determination, trust, and figuring out what comes next.

And that’s part of what makes ROUTE ZERO: The CALLING an interesting moment in their career.

Leaving HOUSE OF TRICKY Behind Without Leaving Themselves Behind

The album marks a major step beyond the HOUSE OF TRICKY storyline. But speaking to Rolling Stone India, the members don’t see it as a reset or a dramatic reinvention. Instead, they return to ideas of growth, ownership, and self-understanding. If the last few years were spent exploring different possibilities, ROUTE ZERO: The CALLING (built around the idea of starting from zero) feels like the point where those experiences begin to come into focus.

According to MINJAE, this chapter is the result of everything they learned while building the HOUSE OF TRICKY series.

From the mischievous energy of early tracks like “TRICKY HOUSE” and “DO or DIE” to the trial-and-error experimentation of “We Don’t Stop” and the darker trap, rock, and cyberpunk textures of WATCH OUT, SPUR, and WRECKING THE HOUSE, xikers have spent six EPs exploring different sounds and concepts. With each release, they’ve moved closer to figuring out what feels most natural to them. “Those experiences have helped us get to know and understand ourselves on a deeper level, from the sounds that suit us best to the styles that truly represent us,” he says. “We felt it was the right time for xikers to take a new step forward and begin a new chapter.”

He emphasizes that now it’s about understanding their identity more clearly. “It’s not that our previous eras weren’t xikers-like. Rather, we want to highlight how xikers, as a group, are now stepping into a new phase, taking greater ownership of our journey and moving forward with a more defined sense of identity, direction, and purpose.”

For JUNGHOON as well, starting from zero meant wiping the slate clean with a renewed mindset and a resolve to refocus. “We wanted to keep the musical identity that xikers has built so far while adding something fresh and showing a different side of xikers.”

What Makes xikers Who They Are?

What separates xikers from the growing pack of fifth-generation boy groups? “I think one of the things that makes xikers special is our raw, unrestrained energy,” HYUNWOO says.

In an industry where identity is often discussed through concepts and branding, energy has long been one of xikers’ defining traits. It first came to light during their 2022 pre-debut training series Ready to One and became clearer when they launched their maiden world tour, TRICKY HOUSE: FIRST ENCOUNTER, earning the nickname “performance powerhouses.” The momentum translated offstage as well, with their album HOUSE OF TRICKY: Doorbell Ringing entering the Billboard 200 at No. 75 and topping Billboard’s Emerging Artists chart within two weeks of release. Whether on international stages or in the studio—where members MINJAE, SUMIN, and YECHAN have held writing credits on nearly every release—it’s the throughline that keeps their music unmistakably theirs, even as they shift from the traditional Korean dokkaebi themes of “TRICKY HOUSE” to heavier rock and trap textures.

For HYUNWOO, that energy is inseparable from the strengths, quirks, and charms each member brings to the outfit. “I think being able to showcase all 10 sides is what makes xikers special.” Their individualities shine through in the interplay between hard-hitting rap, soaring vocals, and theatrical dance breaks. A similar dynamic runs through much of ROUTE ZERO: The CALLING. Led by the title track “DIENAMITE” and accompanied by songs like “Mask Off” and “DUMB,” the record channels their intensity into a sleeker, post-HOUSE OF TRICKY sound, leaning into cleaner production, tighter pacing, and a pop-rap and rock mix of electric guitars, hip-hop grooves, and retro synths.

Growing Into Their Own Voices

The rap line has always sat at the core of xikers’ identity. And as their sound evolves, so does their approach to writing and performing. For SUMIN, songwriting has become a way of documenting growth in real time, with every new experience leaving its mark on his storytelling. “As I’ve been doing more and more songwriting, I’ve naturally learned to look at my work more objectively. I try my best to be honest in my writing and express what I see and feel as truthfully as possible.” More than anything, he wants to stay true to the spirit that first drew him to hip-hop, one that, in his words, “is all about telling your own story honestly.”

While SUMIN focuses on honest self-expression, YECHAN is already thinking about the audience. “Whenever I work on music, I imagine myself on stage and try to create something that makes people think, ‘They’re good,’ ‘This is fun,’ or ‘This is fresh’ as soon as they hear it. Since xikers is a group with a lot to offer performance-wise, I want to bring out that signature powerful energy that makes us who we are while continuing to challenge ourselves with new things.”

On ROUTE ZERO, that sense of creative ownership runs deeper than ever. Having MINJAE co-write and co-compose “DIENAMITE” made the recording process feel different for JINSIK. “I think I felt a little more pressure and responsibility to do well. But those feelings actually became a positive source of motivation and helped us bring even more of ourselves into the song,” he says. For SEEUN, the album’s significance extends beyond the music itself. Arriving at a pivotal moment in the group’s evolution, it represents an important turning point and “holds great significance for us.”

The View from ROUTE ZERO

If ROUTE ZERO: The CALLING is a new beginning for xikers, it’s also a glimpse into how they see themselves and the future of K-pop. With the genre expanding across the world and crossing cultural and musical boundaries, HUNTER feels experimentation and authenticity are two sides of the same coin. “I think one of the exciting things about K-pop is how it continues to evolve by embracing different genres and musical influences.” For xikers, that meant exploring styles such as punk and glam rock on ROUTE ZERO while filtering them through the group’s own perspective. “We’re always looking for new ways to challenge ourselves musically and expand our sound, but it’s equally important for us to stay true to who we are as a group.” The philosophy mirrors much of the conversation surrounding the album itself: change not as a departure from the past, but as a clearer picture of who they have become.

That same perspective is reflected in what the members hope listeners take away from the record. JUNMIN hopes people see a group that doesn’t need “anything extra or anything embellished to stand out.” “We’re cool simply by being ourselves, just as we are.” YUJUN sees the album as an opportunity to showcase a more mature side of xikers. Throughout the conversation, the members rarely settle on a single answer to what makes xikers xikers. Instead, they point to various things: energy, honesty, performance, experimentation, chemistry, sonic growth. For a group that built its reputation within one of fifth-generation K-pop’s most unique narrative universes, that’s perhaps the most revealing takeaway. The members may be moving beyond HOUSE OF TRICKY, but they’re not replacing it with a simpler definition of themselves. If anything, ROUTE ZERO: The CALLING suggests the opposite: the more xikers grow, the harder they become to reduce to any one idea.
